title: Rainwater Puddles
body:
Raindrops fall one at a time on cells of an m × n grid. A wet cell joins any wet cells next to it (up, down, left, right) into one puddle. After every drop, print the number of puddles. A drop can land on a cell that is already wet.

The report only summarised this as a DSU puddle question; this mock uses the standard "Number of Islands II" form.

Function to complete

Complete countPuddles(m, n, cells). It returns the number of puddles after each cell fills.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: Line 1: m n k. Next k lines: r c (0-indexed).

samples.ex: The second drop joins the first; the third and fourth start new puddles.
A repeat drop changes nothing; (1,1) is only diagonal to (0,0).

py.pre:
from typing import *
import sys, math, collections, heapq, bisect, itertools, functools
from collections import *
py.post:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    _raw = sys.stdin.read(); _t = _raw.split(); _p = 0
    m = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    n = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    _k = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    cells = [list(map(int, _t[_p + _i * 2:_p + (_i + 1) * 2])) for _i in range((_k))]; _p += (_k) * 2
    _r = Solution().countPuddles(m, n, cells)
    print(" ".join(map(str, _r)))
